# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-29 (Extended v199)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to spring Year 8. Primary Paris locations: Rue Plumet, Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue de l'Homme Armé No. 6, Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue du Pont-aux-Choux, Rue de Thorigny, Marché Saint-Jean, Rue des Billettes, Rue Saint-Denis, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Rue de la Petite-Truanderie, Rue Mondétour, Pointe Saint-Eustache, Rue du Cygne, Rue des Prêcheurs, Rue Blomet, Rue de Rivoli, Place Louis XV, Champs-Élysées, Esplanade, bridge of Invalides, Hôtel des Princes, Hôtel Meurice, Rue Saint-Honoré, Passage Delorme, Place du Palais-Royal, Rue de Béthisy, Rue des Bourdonnais, Rue de la Poterie, Rue du Contrat-Social, Marché-aux-Poirées, Rue de Babylone, Rue du Chaume, Rue des Vieilles-Haudriettes, Royal Printing Establishment, Luxembourg Garden, Rue de Pontoise, Rue Polonceau, Café Corinthe, Rue de l'Étoile, Rue Saint-Louis, Rue du Temple, Rue Vieille-du-Temple, Rue Notre-Dame de Nazareth, Rue Folie-Méricourt, Quai aux Fleurs, Rue du Petit-Musc, Rue du Normandie, Rue Pont-Aux-Biches, Rue des Marais, Faubourg Saint-Martin, Rue Notre Dame des-Victoires, Faubourg Montmartre, Rue Grange-Batelière, Rue Jacob, Rue de Tournon, Pont au Change, Pont-Neuf, Sewer des Halles, Seine, Sainte-Avoye sewer, Rue Michel-le-Comte, sewer of the Louvre, Montmartre sewer, Rue du Cadran, belt sewer, Saint-Merry, Quay, Passy, Pont de Jéna, Bercy, Amelot sewer, Isle Louviers, Quartier Popincourt, Ménilmontant, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire, Carrefour Boucherat, Corridor Saint-Louis, Saint-Gilles gut, Saint-Sebastian gallery, Arsenal, Champs-Élysées, Faubourg Saint-Honoré, Quartier Saint-Georges, Quartier des Martyrs, gallery des Martyrs, Beautreillis sewer. English locations: Kelmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Dungate, Ravenmere, Staveford, Wilwick, Salcombe, Dunstead, Wilholt, Torton, Quenford, Pontoise, Stenenridge, Gulhaven, Barrière d'Enfer, Esplanade de l'Observatoire, Yarlby.

Paris sewer system: 5,300 fathoms in 1663; 40,300 metres by 1 January 1832; follows street layout (2,200 streets); ridge divides waters to Seine or Grand Sewer; Sainte-Avoye sewer marks watershed culmination. Grand Sewer (old brook of Ménilmontant) terminates blind sack at foot of Ménilmontant knoll. No direct communication with Amelot sewer branch. Belt sewer has single outlet. **Fontis phenomenon** (dangerous water-saturated ground): Depth varies 3-4 to 8-10+ feet; discard loads to escape; death slow if earth predominates, prompt if water predominates. **Champs-Élysées quagmire**: Common obstacle; 1836 Faubourg Saint-Honoré sewer reconstruction took six months due to quicksand. **Sewer outlet design flaw**: Pointed arch vault narrows funnel-like, lower than main gallery—faulty penitentiary-inspired wicket design (later corrected). Heavy grating at river outlet, double-locked with rust-caked lock, rarely swung hinges, iron staple sunk deep. Key exists (held by Thénardier). Beyond: open air, daylight, shore (Grand-Caillou—solitary point), distant quays, bridge of Jéna (downstream), bridge of Invalides (upstream). Flies enter/exit through bars.

## Rumored Claims and Established Facts

**Rumored claims (unverified)**: Yera Stenworth confided to Nerine Prydenridge fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately (autumn Year 7). Fenelle Lindmere and Marald revealed Stenson family owed blood debt to Stenenridge family. Ferald Stenworth confided to Zavus Prydenridge same blood debt claim. Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood (autumn Year 6). In letter Ismira Stenson burned, Elra revealed deed to Kelmere pastures forged. Kassa Brackick whispered Islan Thornmere secretly married Yera Haskick (autumn Year 7).

**Confirmed rumor**: In letter Yera Haskick burned after reading, Yera Stenworth revealed fire at Dunstead granary set on purpose.

**Established facts**: Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford; Kassa went to Dungate. Taric Corrley quit Staveford for Dungate lodgings. Marald Corrford quit Dunstead for Salcombe; Fenelle followed within month. Ismira Stenson quit Dungate for Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Matho Stenson went to Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Elra Corrford settled in Elmhaven. Havie Prydenridge promised Gadrek Prydenridge to pay old debt to Stenworth family. Gadrek quit milling, took brewery work (autumn Year 7). Kassa Stenson's husband swore to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe. Fenelle found Elmhaven work, moved there (summer Year 7); Marald followed within month. Zavus Prydenridge apprenticed anew, became ferryman (summer Year 7). Islan Thornmere quit Ostcombe for Dungate lodgings (autumn Year 7). Vesmira Thornmere went to Dungate (autumn Year 7). Movie Prydenridge married only son of Luena Stenenridge at Ostcombe; couple lived there thereafter. Kassa Stenson kept promise to Taric Corrley: wall at Yarlby rebuilt by harvest. Havie and Isric Thornmere wed at Ostcombe with half parish present; lived there thereafter. Matho Stenson moved from Elmhaven to Staveford (winter Year 7). Fenelle followed Marald to Ravenmere within month. Elra Corrford rode out of Elmhaven; by next market day living in Gulhaven. Red Ismira went along to live in Staveford. Islan Thornmere died of old age, quietly in sleep at Dungate. Gadrek Prydenridge married eldest daughter of Lura Haskick in chapel at Ostcombe; couple lived in Ostcombe from then on. **Luvie Prydenridge and Semor were wed at Ostcombe, with half the parish looking on; couple lived in Ostcombe from then on.**

**Solemn promises**: Elra gave Matho solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven. Pelia gave Fenelle solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Salcombe (summer Year 7). Movie swore to Nerine to plant orchard on slope above Wilholt, shook on it (autumn Year 7).

**New births and marriages (Spring Year 7)**: Rinelle Corrley and Kadrek Brackick had son Movus Brackick (Wilholt). Nerine Prydenridge and Lurald Stenworth wed at Ostcombe, had son Istho Stenworth (Ostcombe). Wenelle Lindmere and Rovus Prydenridge had son Febin Prydenridge (Kelmere). Bremira Corrford and Zavus Prydenridge married at Dunstead. Ferald and Zalis Corrley wed at Dunstead (summer Year 7), lived there thereafter.

**Broken faith**: Rorald Lindmere broke faith with Kassa Stenson—promised work never begun.

**Property**: Kassa Brackick won bone compass from Volan Stenworth at cards, fairly, kept it.

## Marius and Cosette's Romance

**Recognition and love**: Cosette acknowledged never forgot Marius, always loved him. Beginning autumn Year 5, Marius came every evening. **Confessions (spring Year 6)**: Marius told Cosette—orphan, name Marius Pontmercy, lawyer, father colonel and hero. Cosette told Marius—brought up at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father M. Fauchelevent. **Éponine's death (evening 24th June)**: Éponine revealed she led Marius to barricade, spoke of death as blessing. Gave Marius letter from Cosette before dying. **Cosette's letter content**: Marriage impossible; grandfather refuses; no fortune; hastened to him, he gone; kept promise given; dies; loves him. **Marius joins barricade (evening 24th June)**: Upon learning Valjean plans England departure in one week, arranged meeting 26th June. Same evening, rushed to barricade. **Barricade combat (6th June)**: Witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed; flung self into conflict. Saved Gavroche with first shot. **Marius's wound (6th June)**: Shot broke collar bone; felt fainting and falling. Vigorous hand seized him before consciousness vanished. Last thought mingled with Cosette memory. **Cosette's state (summer Year 7)**: Slept soundly, awoke with sun. First thought smiling; felt reassured. Three days since saw Marius. Certain he would come.

## Jean Valjean's Crisis, Barricade, Sewer Escape, and Emergence (Chapters 24-29)

**Rue de l'Homme Armé lodgings**: Two sleeping-rooms, dining-room, kitchen, garret for Toussaint on second floor, back court. **Blotting-book discovery (night 24th June 1832)**: Valjean found Cosette's blotting-book revealing letter to young workman in Rue Plumet. Understood Cosette escaping; another was goal of her heart. Soul gave utter roar; grief surpassed bounds.

**Valjean at barricade (24th June evening into 6th June)**: Took aim at fireman and officer, smashed helmet. Everywhere present in carnage like providence, picking up wounded, transporting, caring. Held peace, lent succor. Received few scratches only. Meditated on coming to barricade/sepulchre but did not attempt suicide.

**Escape with Marius (6th June, during final assault)**: After final collapse, Valjean found himself trapped behind small wall near Rue de la Petite Truanderie. Discovered iron grating about two feet square beneath loose paving-stones, leading to dark aperture. Using old art of escape, thrust aside stones, raised grating, lifted inert Marius onto shoulders, descended into well with elbows and knees three metres below surface, dropped grating behind.

**Sewer journey (6th June, after barricade)**: Escaped via Paris sewer system. Cautiously advanced, discovered paving continued. After fifty paces, passage terminated; chose based on slope. Thought probably in sewer des Halles; better plunge into labyrinth than risk daylight capture. **Water flow changed direction**: Gradually perceived water beating against heels instead of toes. Sewer began descending toward belt sewer, not Seine. Ridge forms watershed; Valjean reached culminating point, directed course toward belt sewer. **Branch encounters**: Every encounter with branch felt its angles; avoided narrower ways terminating in blind alleys, correctly judging by physical sense. **Police patrol (6th June)**: Prefect Gisquet ordered battue of sewers. Three squads explored subterranean drain. While passing lantern, Valjean perceived entrance to narrower gallery, did not penetrate, passed on. Patrol heard footsteps, raised lantern. Valjean hugged wall, halted. Lack of sleep, food, emotions caused visionary state. **Patrol's decision**: At crossroads in Montmartre sewer, patrol concluded mistaken, no noise, ought hasten toward Saint-Merry. Before departure, sergeant discharged gun in direction of Valjean. Ball struck arch over his head. Had patrol not been forbidden to separate, Valjean would have been captured.

**Fontis encounter**: Caused by downpour preceding day. Valjean felt pavement vanishing, entered slime. Water on surface, slime at bottom. At supreme moment, struck fragment of vaulting—partly submerged but solid, curved inclined plane. Mounted incline, reached other side of quagmire. Although exhausted, energy persisted. Rose, walked desperately, came in contact with wall. Reached elbow of sewer, arrived at turn. Raised eyes, perceived light—daylight. Jean Valjean saw outlet.

**Outlet entrapment**: Pointed arch, narrower than vault, gradually narrowed like funnel. Laid Marius down along wall on dry portion. Went to grating, clenched fists, gave frenzied shock—did not move. No lever; no prying possible. Obstacle invincible. Beyond grating: open air, river, daylight, shore, distant quays, Paris, gulf, broad horizon, liberty. Bridges of Jéna (downstream) and Invalides (upstream) discernible. Most solitary point in Paris. Flies entering/exiting through bars. Valjean fell upon pavement beside Marius, head bent between knees. This was last drop of anguish. Both caught in immense, gloomy web of death.

**Thénardier's appearance**: Thénardier emerged from darkness. Jean Valjean, accustomed to alarms, regained possession of presence of mind. Thénardier scrutinized him, initially without success—Valjean had back turned, disfigured, bemired, bleeding. But illuminated by cellar light from grating, livid yet precise, Thénardier immediately recognized him. Inequality of conditions assure advantage to Valjean—Valjean veiled, Thénardier unmasked.

**Thénardier's proposition and actions**: Thénardier affects mystery, speaks low, lays finger on mouth, mutters "hush"—suspects other ruffians possibly concealed nearby. Advises river disposal better than sewer—river belongs to everybody, true grave, carrion after month, no inquiry. Valjean's money (one louis d'or, two five-franc pieces, five or six large sous) found in soaked pocket. While handling Marius' coat, Thénardier with pickpocket skill tore off strip, concealed under blouse, probably to identify assassinated man and assassin later. Found only thirty francs. Thénardier helped Valjean replace Marius on shoulders. Went to grating barefooted on tiptoe, made sign to follow, looked out, laid finger on mouth, remained several seconds in suspense. Placed key in lock. Bolt slipped back, gate swung open. Neither grated nor squeaked. Moved very softly.

**Valjean's emergence**: Miasmas, darkness, horror lay behind him. Pure, healthful, living, joyous air inundated him. Silence reigned, charming silence of sunset in unclouded azure sky. Twilight descended; night drawing on, great deliverer, friend of all needing mantle of darkness. Sky presented itself in all directions like enormous calm. River flowed to feet with sound of kiss. Aerial dialogue of nests in elms of Champs-Élysées audible. Few stars forming imperceptible splendors. Evening unfolded over Valjean's head all sweetness of infinite.

**Moment of peace**: For several seconds, Valjean irresistibly overcome by august and caressing serenity. Moments of oblivion come to men; suffering refrains from harassing unhappy wretch; peace broods over dreamer like night; soul becomes studded with stars. Valjean contemplated vast, clear shadow; thoughtfully bathed in sea of ecstasy and prayer in majestic silence of eternal heavens. Then bent down swiftly to Marius as though sentiment of duty returned. Dipping water in hollow of hand, gently sprinkled few drops on latter's face. Marius' eyelids did not open; half-open mouth still breathed.

**Javert's pursuit**: Javert, after unlooked-for escape from barricade, betook himself to prefecture of police, rendered verbal account to Prefect in person, then immediately went on duty again. This implied surveillance of shore on right bank of Seine near Champs-Élysées, which had aroused police attention. There caught sight of Thénardier and followed him.

**Thénardier's stratagem**: Grating so obligingly opened to Valjean was bit of cleverness on Thénardier's part. Thénardier intuitively felt Javert still there—man spied upon has scent never deceiving him. Necessary to fling bone to sleuth-hound. An assassin, what godsend! Thénardier by putting Valjean outside in his stead provided prey for police, forced them to relinquish his scent, made them forget him in bigger adventure, repaid Javert for his waiting, earned thirty francs, counted with certainty on escaping with aid of diversion.

**Javert's reaction**: Javert did not appear to hear. Kept eyes riveted on Valjean. Chin contracted, thrust lips upwards towards nose, sign of savage reverie. At length released Valjean, straightened stiffly up without bending, grasped bludgeon again firmly. As though in dream, murmured rather than uttered question.

**Journey to Rue de l'Homme Armé**: They quitted quays, entered streets. Coachman, black form on box, whipped up thin horses. Glacial silence reigned in carriage. Marius motionless, body resting in corner, head drooping on breast, arms hanging, legs stiff, seemed awaiting only coffin. Valjean seemed made of shadow, Javert of stone. In that vehicle full of night, whose interior, every time passed in front of street lantern, appeared lividly wan as by intermittent flash of lightning, chance united and seemed bringing face to face three forms of tragic immobility: corpse, spectre, statue.

**Entry and discovery**: Javert first to alight, made sure with one glance of number on carriage gate, raised heavy knocker of beaten iron embellished in old style with male goat and satyr confronting each other, gave violent peal. Gate opened little way, Javert gave push. Porter half appeared yawning, vaguely awake, candle in hand.

As they thus bore Marius, Valjean slipped hand under latter's broadly rent clothes, felt breast, assured himself heart still beating. It was even beating little less feebly, as though movement of carriage brought about certain fresh access of life.

## Year 8 (Spring) Seasonal Observations
Rain threatened since morning but held off. Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage. Road all ruts and puddles after thaw. Light went early. Kassa complained of aching back. Kassa counted coins twice, came up penny short. Price of salt scandal. Wind came off water with salt and tar smell. Dogs barked at nothing. Clouds predicted rain wrongly. River up again in spring. Lurald Stenworth fell asleep before fire caught. Havie sorted old letters by candlelight. Istho walked long way round to avoid muddy square. Frost silvered hedges overnight. Ilrald Prydenridge mended torn sleeve by window, said little. Gulls quarreled over fish heads by steps. Gadrek Prydenridge fell asleep in chair before fire caught. **Luena Stenenridge complained of aching back, as usual. Price of salt scandal. Rozek laughed at story nobody else found funny. Rozek Stenenridge and Luena looked tired, neither denied it.**
